title: Proximal humerus insertion site
view: Right shoulder and upper arm from the front, patient supine, arm adducted with the hand on the abdomen: lateral on the image left, the chest on the right. Inset: the humeral head from above, anterior up, lateral left.
teachingPoint: Insert on the greater tubercle, the most prominent lateral bony point, with the needle 45 degrees to the anterior plane aimed posteromedially - not straight down at 90 degrees.
claims: Right shoulder from the front, lateral on the image left (house laterality).
Teal: a 1 cm insertion zone on the greater tubercle, below the acromion on the lateral shoulder (record: the most prominent lateral bony point; zone size drawn as at the tibia).
Inset, seen from the head of the bed (anterior up, lateral left): the needle enters the anterolateral greater tubercle at 45 degrees to the dashed anterior plane, aimed posteromedially (record).
Standard anatomy added: acromion about 4 cm above the tubercle, clavicle, deltopectoral groove, the glenoid medial in the inset; arm internally rotated so the tubercle faces anterolaterally.
Labels: Greater tubercle, Acromion, 45°, Anterior plane.

geometry.why: the tubercle is below the acromion
the site is lateral to the deltopectoral groove
inset: the glenoid is medial (medial is right)
inset: the needle tip is at the greater tubercle
inset: the needle runs anterior to posterior at 45 degrees, not 90
inset: the needle enters the tubercle
